tests.description: a double quote in a path
tests.comment: RFC 3986, Appendix A: pchar = unreserved / pct-encoded / sub-delims / ":" / "@", and the double quote is in none of them.
RFC 3986, Section 3.2.2: square brackets are reserved for an IP-literal inside the authority. path-absolute is built from pchar, which excludes them.

tests.description: a non-numeric port in a network-path reference
tests.comment: RFC 3986, Section 3.2.3: port = *DIGIT. reg-name admits no colon, so the text after the colon can only be a port.

tests.description: more than one at-sign in the authority
tests.comment: RFC 3986, Section 3.2: authority = [ userinfo "@" ] host [ ":" port ]. Neither userinfo nor host admits a literal at-sign.

tests.description: a leading zero in the IPv4 part of an IPv6 literal
tests.comment: RFC 3986, Section 3.2.2: inside an IP-literal the dotted quad must be an IPv4address, and dec-octet has no leading-zero alternative. There is no reg-name fallback inside brackets.

tests.description: a colon in the first segment of a relative-path reference
tests.comment: RFC 3986, Section 4.2: relative-part uses path-noscheme, whose first segment is segment-nz-nc - a non-zero-length segment without any colon. A scheme must start with ALPHA, so 1:b cannot be read as a URI either.
